holds.excerpt: A cracked ringland is confirmed by a leakdown/compression test on the affected cylinder;
A/C clutch relay and pressure switch should be tested before assuming compressor failure.

Out of warranty/recall, the switch itself is an inexpensive part (~$30-50) but diagnosis of a no-start or no-shift complaint is often misattributed to the battery, starter, or ignition before the switch is found.
budget for intermittent stalling diagnosis since the failure can be load/temperature dependent and may not store a code.
Replace both head gaskets with updated multi-layer-steel gaskets, resurface/pressure-test the heads, and replace the timing belt, water pump, and thermostat while the front of the engine is open.
Diagnosis typically starts with scanning for cooling-system related DTCs and confirming abnormal coolant temperature behavior or heater output.
Test the lockup solenoid;
If you experience harsh/delayed engagement, flaring, jerking, or a transmission warning, scan for CVT codes and get it evaluated quickly.
Out of warranty, a rebuilt/updated valve body is far cheaper than a complete CVT unit — get a diagnosis of the specific failed component before authorizing a full replacement.
test whether the fan runs on HIGH only (points to the resistor on manual systems, or the power transistor on auto-climate cars);
Auto-climate cars with no fan and a dead A/C light may need control-head diagnosis.
Diagnose by pouring a small amount of water into the sunroof channel corners and watching where it exits — it should drain out below each A-pillar/rocker, not into the cabin.
If consumption test confirms issue, piston ring replacement may be covered.
Pressure-test/UV-dye the system to locate the leak, then replace the leaking A/C condenser (or repair the damaged line / failed O-ring), evacuate and recharge the system.
Diagnosis usually begins with stored cooling-system related DTCs and confirmation of improper thermo control valve operation using scan data.
document the source (video/audio) to speed diagnosis.
Diagnosis usually starts with scanning for secondary air system codes and commanding the pump/valves with a capable scan tool.
Perform a boost leak test with a pressure tester ($30-$50 DIY tool).
Pressure test the charge system;

releaseBlockers.reason: The make audit completed with explicit holds only; there is no reviewed part-link write to release.
